source.title: Separation or binding? Role of the dentate gyrus in hippocampal mnemonic processing

confidence_rationale: This entry exists to prevent the pull from being a one-sided case for the mechanism the V3-EXQ-898 autopsy already favoured, and it is the strongest available statement of the dissenting position: that the theoretical support and empirical evidence for the DG-as-pattern-separator theory 'are not strong', and that 'binding' of different types of incoming sensory information better captures the DG's contribution to memory encoding. Its direct relevance to SD-016 is sharp, because BINDING is arguably a better description of what SD-016's ContextMemory is actually for -- associating a context cue with hazard-relevant content -- than separation is. Confidence 0.61 rather than higher because this is a minority position argued in a review rather than demonstrated with new data, it predates the strongest connectivity evidence in this pull (Espinoza 2018) which materially strengthens the case it argues against, and the authors' positive alternative (binding) is specified far less precisely than the theory they criticise -- which limits how much design guidance it can actually supply. It is weighted here as a genuine and well-argued caution, not as a refutation.
failure_signatures: The core critique is that 'pattern separation' as used in the behavioural literature (discriminating similar contexts) and as defined computationally (orthogonalising overlapping input patterns) are DIFFERENT claims routinely conflated. SD-016's C1b context-divergence instrument measures the computational sense; the claim's actual functional motivation (vmPFC-like anticipatory hazard response) is behavioural. A pass on the computational instrument does not establish the behavioural function, and the two must not be reported as if they were one result.

If the DG's primary role is BINDING rather than separation, then engineering competitive/sparsifying dynamics into SD-016's retrieval could be actively counterproductive -- sparsification discards the conjunctive combination of inputs that binding requires. The H3 leg would then be expected to produce low entropy AND degraded downstream terrain/action performance, which is a specific, falsifiable prediction worth instrumenting for rather than a vague caution.

The authors conclude the empirical evidence for pattern separation is 'not strong', which means the biological-reference triage in the V3-EXQ-898 autopsy rests on a contested rather than settled literature. The autopsy's framing of the REE tagger as a 'formal-definition import' of pattern separation may therefore be importing a definition whose biological reality is itself disputed.

Much of the behavioural evidence for DG pattern separation comes from adult-neurogenesis manipulations, which have effects on excitability, network sparsity and mood-related behaviour beyond any separation-specific role -- so the causal attribution to separation specifically is weaker than the literature's confident vocabulary suggests.

mapping.source_claim_statement: A currently popular theory proposes that the primary function of the dentate gyrus is to orthogonalise incoming input patterns into non-overlapping patterns (pattern separation). The authors critically review the available data and conclude that the theoretical support and empirical evidence for this theory are not strong. They then review an alternative theory positing a role for the DG in BINDING TOGETHER different types of incoming sensory information, and conclude that 'binding' better captures the contribution of the DG to memory encoding than 'pattern separation'.
mapping.ree_translation: This is the entry that argues the SD-016 fix direction may be misdiagnosed at the root. The GOV-FANOUT-1 H3 leg proposes hard/competitive selection because the biological reference is pattern separation; if the DG is better described as a conjunctive BINDING stage, the correct import is nearly opposite -- a mechanism that combines z_world with other input streams into a conjunctive code, rather than one that sparsifies and orthogonalises. That reading is not idle for SD-016 specifically, because SD-016's own functional_restatement describes a binding job in all but name: associate an exteroceptive context cue with hazard-relevant content so that E2 affordance and E3 terrain precision can be modulated before harm contact. Nothing in that description requires orthogonalisation; it requires a reliable conjunction. Practical consequence: the H3 leg should instrument DOWNSTREAM function (terrain_loss, and where possible action_bias divergence) alongside C1/C1b, so that a 'successful' entropy drop accompanied by degraded downstream performance is DETECTED as the binding-critique's predicted signature rather than reported as a partial win. This costs nothing to add and converts a philosophical caveat into a discriminating measurement.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This is a minority position argued in a review, not demonstrated with new data, and it should not be given equal weight to the direct measurements in this directory. It predates Espinoza et al. 2018, whose connectivity results materially strengthen the case for the WTA/separation architecture the authors are criticising, so its critique is not fully informed by the current best evidence. The positive alternative is also considerably less well specified than the theory it displaces -- 'binding' is not operationalised to the point where it yields an implementable REE mechanism, which is precisely why this entry generates an INSTRUMENT recommendation rather than a design recommendation. Finally, the separation-versus-binding dispute is partly about the DG's role in a full memory system with encoding and retrieval phases; SD-016 has no encoding phase under test in this lineage, so some of the dispute is orthogonal to what the portfolio can discriminate.
mapping.source_context: Critical review in Neuroscience and Biobehavioral Reviews synthesising rodent lesion, electrophysiology and adult-neurogenesis literature on dentate gyrus function; no new empirical data.

confidence_components.notes: Neuroscience and Biobehavioral Reviews is a solid review venue and the critique is careful and well argued, but it is a minority position without new data and is now superseded in part by later connectivity work; source_quality 0.70. Mapping fidelity 0.62 -- the observation that SD-016's own functional_restatement describes binding rather than separation is a genuinely sharp mapping, but the binding alternative is too under-specified to yield an implementable mechanism, so the entry's actionable output is an instrumentation change rather than a design change. Transfer risk 0.40 reflects that the separation-versus-binding dispute is framed around a full encode-and-retrieve memory system, while SD-016's lineage tests retrieval selection only. Aggregate 0.61: a real and well-argued caution that should shape instrumentation and interpretation, not a refutation that should redirect the portfolio.
